system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s **[STANDARD] labels and reviewer note do not establish Buyer agreement or approval**. All issues remain subject to our playbook; no Amelia Frost approval has been given for conditional fallbacks.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m cap. | 25% / AUD 6m; 20% only with Amelia’s prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject; restore AUD 6m.** The conditional fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, recovering only the excess. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Amend both thresholds and basket mechanics.** Seller’s proposal materially excludes otherwise recoverable losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | 18 months; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | 24 months for general warranties; 18 months requires Amelia’s written approval; no spillover into separate categories. | **Restore 24 months and remove blanket application.** Neither the shorter period nor cross-category limitation is authorised. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share general warranty caps and time limits. | Separate 100% / AUD 24m cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject general-regime treatment.** Ownership and capacity require distinct protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims without a stated exception. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct excluded from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an overriding carve-out throughout.** This protection is mandatory and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Deems the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records disclosed. | Specific fair disclosure sufficient to identify the nature and scope of the relevant matter; no blanket data-room, public-register or prudent-search disclosure. | **Reject general deemed disclosure; assess specific disclosures individually.** Mere availability of information must not defeat warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including discoverable matters. | Delete blanket Buyer-knowledge exclusions; any retained knowledge qualification must use named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, never excusing title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3 as drafted.** It transfers discovery risk to Buyer and undermines negotiated remedies. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, although final consent and condition-satisfaction evidence are absent. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**. | **Make both express Completion requirements.** Consent-on-delivery is inadequate for a customer representing approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release after Completion; no repayment or final discharge evidenced. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. | **Require a documented Completion discharge mechanism.** A post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia’s approval, neither presently established. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses treated as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Specific funds-flow provision or verified Seller funding for DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs. | **Expressly allocate and fund the obligation; confirm triggering conditions and on-costs.** Silent omission risks leaving the acquired company with an unfunded liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity confined to SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 shown open, without independent payment verification, receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Broader indemnity addressing related IP ownership/transfer exposure, while preserving the SOW3 payment-and-transfer cure. | **Broaden protection and obtain payment/vesting evidence.** AUD 180,000 is not independently verified as paid or unpaid, and payment-only protection may miss title-related loss. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter said not to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Preserve logs, investigate access and scope, assess legal obligations and require updates. | **Keep diligence and contractual protections open; require preservation and reporting.** Neither a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty nor any numeric demand is established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing, scope, accrual, termination rights and unavoidable commitments. | **Reserve classification pending evidence; make no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** The supplied disclosure does not establish the asserted ordinary-course treatment. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations presumptively apply to all Claims; Tax/IP treated as settled within that regime. | Express separation of Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories, without hidden general-regime overrides. | **Remove catch-all application and specify each regime’s scope and priority.** Blanket drafting could neutralise separately negotiated obligations and remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s internal share register recording Seller’s 100% holding. | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. | **Require independent corroboration and supporting documents.** DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof of clean title or authority. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Says Tax/IP warranty positions are settled under general limitations. | Keep Tax/IP terms open and negotiate their substantive protections and applicable limitations separately. | **Reject the claimed settlement and expressly reserve both categories.** Neither resolution nor unlimited liability may be assumed. |

**Related disclosure points:** DD-007 identifies a lease **notification**, not an established consent requirement; DD-009’s assignment restriction does not itself establish that Mossvale consent is required for the share sale.
=== END ADVICE ===
